title: Making Disciples at the Table
subtitle: Discipleship without a program — four essays, a study, and a book.
forWhom: For the ordinary Christian with no title and no training who suspects that following Jesus was always meant to be handed on, not just attended.

movements.heading: Read these first
movements.note: Start with why attendance is not discipleship, then move to the table Jesus actually used and the formation happening to you whether you chose it or not.

items.label: Building a Culture of Discipleship, Not Just Attendance
items.blurb: A full building on Sunday can still make no disciples. The metrics lie.

items.label: The Meal That Was Supposed to Make Us One
items.blurb: The table Jesus left to unite us became the thing we argue over. Recovering the point.

items.label: Why Just Agreeing With Jesus Isn't Enough
items.blurb: Assent is not apprenticeship. He asked for followers, not fans.

items.label: The Machine That Forms You
items.blurb: You are being discipled every day — by a feed, if not by a person.

movements.heading: Then set a table
movements.note: The Basics at the Table is a guided study for starting with one person — the meal, the text, the question, and the sending, the way Jesus taught it.

items.label: The Basics at the Table — a study for disciplers
items.blurb: A work-through study that ends with you discipling someone by name.

movements.heading: Then read the book, free
movements.note: Come to the Table recovers Jesus's method for people with no training: disciple-making in ordinary homes. By the last chapter you will have set your first table. Free to read.

items.label: Come to the Table — read free
items.blurb: Twelve chapters on disciple making in homes for ordinary Christians. The complete book, free.

items.label: Find James's books in the bookstore
items.blurb: Print and ebook editions of the full library.
